Watching AI stocks absolutely puke is a reminder about how beautifully timed Anthropic’s IPO was. Now that it’s done, the worse the capital markets get, the better it is for Anthropic.

Post-IPO, $ANT has nearly $250 billion of cash on its balance sheet, a cash flow breakeven (or better) business, and the possibility its main rival may be stuck private, cash-burning, undercapitalized, and incapable of cracking compute-efficiency the way Anthropic has.

At the same time, Anthropic’s suppliers are now staring into a late-2027 compute glut, the supply of which basically can’t be stopped given existing inertial forces. That could leave Anthropic sitting pretty as a renter with spot market exposure - picture Eddie Murphy and Dan Akroyd at the end of Trading Places, standing calmly in the pits taking orders from desperate counterparties.

In fact, Anthropic has every motivation to encourage and FACILITATE a glut.

The worse the capital market environment gets, the better it is for Anthropic’s long-term prospects.

en_summary: Presented $MRVL for $LITE merger as example of what goes wrong using own stock to buy another. MRVL dropped -45% in over a month, cutting +24% premium for LITE to -41% discount. Massive dilution and arbitragers. Same dynamic likely when $SPCX offers +24% premium for $TSLA using SPCX stock: short-term pop then downward pressure. LITE now down -41% to $535 from $914 pre-deal. TSLA at $374 +24% could be -25% less within a month due to dilution.
text:
I’ve presented the $MRVL - for- $LITE merger proposal as a prime example of what can go wrong when a company uses its own stock to buy another company’s stock.  In just over a month, $MRVL’s stock has dropped by -45%, which has cut the +24% premium being paid for $LITE to a -41% discount vs $LITE’s stock price before the announcement. This occurs because of massive dilution to the acquiring company’s stock, plus arbitragers pre-selling shares of the acquirer rather than wait for the deal to close in 12-18 months.  

The same dynamic is likely when $SPCX offers a +24% premium for $TSLA using SPCX stock as currency:  TSLA investors will get a short-term pop on the deal headline and then experience quick downward pressure on $TSLA stock as investors sell $SPCX to try to lock in profits.

I would bet most $LITE investors would love to roll back the clock to Oct 28 when their stock was trading at $914 before MRVL’s offer to pay a +24% premium which on paper amounted to $1,132/share ($914 + 24%).  Instead $LITE stock is now DOWN -41% since the deal announcement to just $535/share today (-41% from $914 instead of a +24% premium).  If history repeats, TSLA at $374 today plus a +24% premium paid in SPCX shares (on paper worth $464/share) could be worth -25% less within a month ($280/share) given what could amount to 50% dilution to $SPCX, which could trade down by less than $MRVL since it’s not a pure AI play.
